title: הערוץ — four ways to play it
question: You picked the Channel, so the family is settled: the week is an instrument made of light inside a pressed channel, in the one material. What is still open is what that instrument measures and where it sits. The first card is what you already picked, unchanged, so the others have something to beat.

options.label: הערוץ · what you picked
options.thesis: One horizontal channel across the top, filled by the week's sessions, and the doors as a pressed grid of chips.
options.viewport: The channel, the slab that starts a workout, then six doors in two columns raised out of one trough.
options.risk: One long bar says how many, never which days — a week of three sessions all on Monday reads identically to three spread out.

options.label: שבע מבחנות · Seven Tubes
options.thesis: Seven short vertical channels, one per day, each filled by what that day held — the nutrition screen's own signature, so the two screens are the same instrument.
options.viewport: Seven tubes across the top with the day letters beneath, Sunday leading on the right; today's tube is lit amber. Then the slab, then four doors.
options.risk: Seven tubes is more furniture than one bar, and four doors fit above the fold where six did — two of them move down.

options.label: ערוץ ושורות · Channel and Rows
options.thesis: The same channel, but every door says its own state instead of a caption: tomorrow is legs, 65kg on the bench, 7,240 steps today.
options.viewport: The channel, the slab, then all six doors as full-width rows in a single pressed list, each carrying one fact in small type where the caption used to be.
options.risk: A door with nothing to say yet has to say something — the first week, six rows read as six empty promises.

options.label: הפס · The Band
options.thesis: The channel stops being an element and becomes the page's own top edge, full bleed, with the slab inverted — pressed into the page with one raised button on it.
options.viewport: A 46px band of light across the very top with hairline day ticks in it, the title beneath it, then the workout pressed into the page with a round raised button, then six doors.
options.risk: It spends the screen's strongest position on the week, and the workout — the thing 90% of visits came for — is no longer the first thing raised out of the page.
